candidates.quote: Have courage to use your own reason!
candidates.author: Immanuel Kant
candidates.work: An Answer to the Question: What Is Enlightenment?
candidates.whyThisMonth: The month’s whole difficulty in one imperative, because Kant puts the failure where it actually sits, in resolution rather than in understanding.

candidates.quote: That which does not kill me, makes me stronger.
candidates.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
candidates.whyThisMonth: The one aphorism the whole theme is built on, and it describes nothing, it only refuses to let the difficulty count as damage.

candidates.quote: I should say that courage is a sort of endurance of the soul, if I am to speak of the universal nature which pervades them all.
candidates.author: Plato
candidates.speaker: Laches
candidates.whyThisMonth: Endurance of the soul is the plainest account of courage anyone has given, and Socrates at once asks whether endurance without wisdom counts, which is the honest question a hard morning raises.

candidates.quote: But all things excellent are as difficult as they are rare.
candidates.author: Baruch Spinoza
candidates.locator: Part V, Note to Proposition XLII, the closing sentence of the book
candidates.whyThisMonth: The last sentence of the Ethics says the difficulty you are feeling is the price of the thing being worth having, not evidence that you have taken a wrong turn.

candidates.quote: Nevertheless, not to extinguish our free will, I hold it to be true that Fortune is the arbiter of one-half of our actions, but that she still leaves us to direct the other half, or perhaps a little less.
candidates.author: Niccolò Machiavelli
candidates.whyThisMonth: Half is out of your hands and half is not, which is a bracing division to make at six in the morning when the whole day looks like fate.

candidates.quote: Man is but a reed, the most feeble thing in nature; but he is a thinking reed.
candidates.author: Blaise Pascal
candidates.whyThisMonth: It grants the frailty before it grants the dignity, so a reader who this morning feels like the most feeble thing in nature is not being argued out of it.

candidates.quote: He said not: Thou shalt not be tempested, thou shalt not be travailed, thou shalt not be afflicted; but He said: Thou shalt not be overcome.
candidates.author: Julian of Norwich
candidates.whyThisMonth: It promises not that the storm will be spared you but that it will not finish you, and the editor should rule whether a devotional treatise by a named author belongs here or in the Prayer tab.

candidates.quote: If all Men are born free, how is it that all Women are born slaves?
candidates.author: Mary Astell
candidates.locator: Preface of 1706, in Astell: Political Writings, ed. Patricia Springborg (1996), p. 18
candidates.whyThisMonth: One question asked out loud where it was not welcome, which is the shape courage most often takes at a desk rather than in a battle.

candidates.quote: These are the times that try men’s souls. The summer soldier and the sunshine patriot will, in this crisis, shrink from the service of their country; but he that stands it now, deserves the love and thanks of man and woman.
candidates.author: Thomas Paine
candidates.locator: opening sentences, in The Writings of Thomas Paine, ed. M. D. Conway, Vol. I (1894)
candidates.whyThisMonth: The sentence the month is named after, and its second half is the consolation; keep the edition named, since Conway sets the first word in capitals and the 1776 printing reads a colon and ‘his country’.

candidates.quote: I do not wish them to have power over men; but over themselves.
candidates.author: Mary Wollstonecraft
candidates.work: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
candidates.locator: chapter 4, Observations on the State of Degradation to Which Woman Is Reduced by Various Causes
candidates.whyThisMonth: Power over oneself is the only power worth wanting on a hard day, and she asks for it without asking anybody else to lose anything.

candidates.quote: I do not care what case you put; let them be sea-captains, if you will.
candidates.author: Margaret Fuller
candidates.locator: Woman in the Nineteenth Century, and Kindred Papers, ed. Arthur B. Fuller (1855), p. 174
candidates.whyThisMonth: A cheerful refusal to agree that a thing is impossible for you, delivered without raising the voice, which is courage in its most usable form.

candidates.quote: But I ask no favors for my sex. I surrender not our claim to equality. All I ask of our brethren is, that they will take their feet from off our necks, and permit us to stand upright on that ground which God designed us to occupy.
candidates.author: Sarah Moore Grimké
candidates.work: Letters on the Equality of the Sexes, and the Condition of Woman
candidates.locator: Letter II, Woman Subject Only to God (Isaac Knapp, 1838), p. 10
candidates.whyThisMonth: A working model of how to hold a position under pressure: no favours asked, no claim surrendered, and the whole request made in a level voice.

candidates.quote: The cause of freedom is not the cause of a race or a sect, a party or a class,—it is the cause of human kind, the very birthright of humanity.
candidates.author: Anna Julia Cooper
candidates.locator: the essay Woman versus the Indian (Aldine Printing House, 1892), pp. 120 to 121
candidates.whyThisMonth: It widens a private trial into a common one, which is the thought that lets a reader keep going after their own reason for going is spent.

candidates.quote: To conquer fear is the beginning of wisdom, in the pursuit of truth as in the endeavor after a worthy manner of life.
candidates.author: Bertrand Russell
candidates.locator: the essay An Outline of Intellectual Rubbish, first printed 1943
candidates.whyThisMonth: It names the enemy correctly and then says conquering it is where wisdom starts rather than where it ends; American printings read endeavor and British ones endeavour, so the edition named decides.

candidates.quote: To will oneself free is also to will others free.
candidates.author: Simone de Beauvoir
candidates.locator: Part II, Personal Freedom and Others
candidates.whyThisMonth: Freedom taken alone turns out not to be freedom, which makes a solitary struggle into something owed to other people and therefore much harder to abandon.

candidates.quote: Courage is indispensable because in politics not life but the world is at stake.
candidates.author: Hannah Arendt
candidates.whyThisMonth: It says why courage is not optional for anyone who wants to act in public at all; the essay stands as the locator because the section number could not be pinned.
